summary: Plan industrial hygiene sampling, interpret exposure evidence, and prioritize controls. Explore the five-day course and practical curriculum.
lede: Occupational exposure assessment helps practitioners plan representative monitoring and connect findings to controls. For occupational hygienists, HSE professionals, plant managers and occupational-health teams, the course covers hazard characterization, similar exposure groups, sampling plans and interpretation across chemical, physical and biological hazards. Participants practise maintaining exposure registers, prioritizing controls, checking laboratory results and documenting risk-based actions, with expert verification emphasized for AI-assisted screening.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for practitioners who plan exposure monitoring, interpret occupational hygiene evidence, or use it to make control and health-surveillance decisions.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with occupational health and safety, industrial operations, or occupational-health practice is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel for spreadsheet-based exercises; Power BI is discussed conceptually and is not required for completion.
